title: Resuspension and Concentration of Iron Chloride Precipitated Viruses from Seawater for HMW DNA Extraction
author: Natalie Solonenko
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b4niqvce

steps.title: Prepare Resuspension Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.2M citrate 0.2M MgCl2 buffer, pH 6-6.5.

substeps.instruction: Add 29.41g sodium citrate and 5.09g magnesium chloride hexahydrate to ~400mL milliQ water.
Adjust pH to 6-6.5 using HCl.
Fill to 500mL with milliQ water.
Autoclave to sterilize and store at 4°C.

steps.title: Prepare Filter and Sample
steps.instruction: Ensure the iron chloride precipitate is accessible to the buffer.

substeps.instruction: Unfold and re-fold filters if they were folded precipitate side in.
If only a portion of the precipitate is needed (e.g., 10L out of 20L), cut the filter and move the required portion to a new tube.
Sterilize scissors and forceps with 10% bleach and rinse with milliQ water.

steps.title: Resuspend Precipitate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the precipitate using the prepared buffer and rotate overnight.

substeps.instruction: Add 1ml buffer for each 1mg Fe (e.g., 20ml of 1x buffer for 20L seawater precipitate).
Place tubes on a rotator and rotate at 4°C overnight (18:00:00).
If significant precipitate remains on the filters, leave the rotator at room temperature for a few hours.

steps.title: Recover Buffer from Filter
steps.instruction: Collect the resuspension liquid from the filter.

substeps.instruction: Using bleached and rinsed forceps, pull an edge of the filter onto the tube edge so it is caught in the lid when secured.
Centrifuge at low speed (less than 1000 rpm) for 3-5 minutes to remove buffer from the filter.
If the filter still has substantial precipitate, add more buffer, incubate again for a couple of hours, and collect liquid.

steps.title: Treat with DNase
steps.instruction: Treat the viral resuspension with DNase following protocol https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.c3myk5.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 1hr at 37°C to aid in more complete dissolving of the viral resuspension.

steps.title: Concentrate Sample via Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Concentrate the sample using a 15mL 100kDa Amicon centrifugal device.

substeps.instruction: Fill the upper reservoir with the sample. If volume exceeds 15mL, empty the bottom reservoir as sample passes through and refill the top until all sample is added.
Centrifuge at 1000-3000g until the level in the upper reservoir is below 250µl.
Start at 1000g for 15 min; continue in 15-30 minute increments.
If little sample passes through in 30 min at 1000g, increase speed to 2000g, then to 3000g if necessary (process usually takes 2-6 hours).

steps.title: Recover Viral Concentrate
steps.instruction: Extract the concentrated virus from the Amicon device using a washing process.

substeps.instruction: Remove the upper reservoir from the Amicon and place the cap on top.
Vortex at ~1,500rpm for 20 sec, tilting the reservoir to each side to maximize resuspension.
Pipet the viral concentrate out of the upper reservoir into a 2mL tube using a 200µl pipettor.
Add 190µl of resuspension buffer to the upper reservoir and repeat the vortexing and pipetting steps to add the recovered concentrate into the same 2mL tube.
Repeat the buffer addition and vortexing process for a total of 3x rounds.

steps.title: Store Sample
steps.instruction: Store the viral concentrate at 4°C and proceed to HMW DNA extraction (https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6cbhasn).
